rationale: A wins because it keeps four real reporter shapes cleanly separated and does not smuggle in a second briefing. Its best line, "The story isn't the feature — it's the fee," is exactly the discipline this update needs. B is competent, but "Epic v. Apple, Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers" imports outside context the prompt did not give, and "servers have historically been free communities" turns a plausible assumption into copy.
gaps_in_A: Minor extra baggage in "Nitro-style subscriptions" inside the IPO proof ask; the update did not supply Discord's current revenue mix or Nitro context.
"The server owners about to find out what their communities are worth" is smart, but it depends entirely on a named operator; A says that clearly, but it is still the thinnest live pitch at launch.

The trend angle asks for "at least one comparable data point or example of community-first monetization" but does not define what comparison would be clean enough to avoid becoming a competitor-soup story.
gaps_in_B: "Epic v. Apple, Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers" is unearned. Those may be relevant context, but they are not in the supplied update, and this is supposed to judge only grounded angles.
"Discord, Patreon, Twitch, Geneva" repeats the same problem: competitor names smuggled into a trend angle without facts, positioning, or responses.

"Discord servers have historically been free communities" is likely true in the real world, but the prompt did not give it. A grounded angle would say paid roles change the server-owner/member relationship, not pretend the history was supplied.
The trend and customer-story material collapse into one angle. B has three usable shapes, but it leaves A's sharper server-owner profile angle on the table.
